summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging, debug and fix a broken Docker build in the API, consolidate the web app's fragmented HTTP client layers, and unblock release-please after it got stuck due to a monorepo config migration.
summary.outcome: Fixed the API Dockerfile (PR #308), consolidated the web app from 3 HTTP client paths + 8800 lines of orval-generated code down to a single api-client with unified 401 refresh (PR #309), fixed several release-please config issues including pull-request-title-pattern and autorelease:pending label management, and identified the IPNS publish latency root cause (fire-and-forget DHT) and token refresh root cause (orval fetch client had no 401 handling).

repo: CipherBox API is zero-knowledge — it never handles plaintext or performs encryption, so it genuinely has no workspace package dependencies. The api-client package is for non-React consumers; the web app had its own duplicate orval generation in react-query mode.

The web app had three separate HTTP client paths: orval react-query hooks (fetch-based custom-instance.ts), a hand-written axios client (lib/api/client.ts for login/vault), and bare fetch in ipfs.ts. Only the axios client had token refresh interceptors.

IPNS publishes were slow because IpnsService.publishRecord() was awaiting delegated routing DHT propagation via the someguy sidecar. DHT propagation takes 10-30s but is unnecessary to await since resolveRecord() always prefers the DB cache.

release-please identifies release PRs by the `autorelease: pending` label, not just title. Manually creating a git tag (without going through release-please) leaves this label stuck, causing all future release-please runs to abort with 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding'.

release-please's default monorepo title pattern includes ${component}, but the root package has no explicit component name, producing titles like 'chore: release main' that cannot be round-tripped through the pattern parser.

The web app's orval react-query hooks were almost entirely unused — only useHealthControllerCheck was used as a hook; all other generated hooks were ignored in favor of the raw generated functions, which are identical to what @cipherbox/api-client exports.
packages/crypto was incorrectly listed in release-please root extra-files, causing its package.json version to be bumped on every release even when no crypto code changed.

The CI verify step was diffing all of packages/api-client/ rather than just the generated paths (openapi.json, src/generated/, src/models/), causing false failures on any manual edit to instance.ts or tests.

code.finding: result variable stays 'success' with fire-and-forget pattern since delegated routing errors no longer mutate it — correct behavior since DB write is the authoritative publish
Deleted — was the orval fetch mutator with no 401 handling, now replaced by api-client's axios instance with interceptor
Added refreshAccessToken callback, withCredentials, onRefreshFailure, and 401 response interceptor with shared-promise deduplication to prevent concurrent refresh storms
New file — single call site for setApiClientConfig() that wires refresh token, withCredentials, and onRefreshFailure (redirect to login) for the entire web app
logout, unlinkMethod, deleteAccount were typed as Promise<unknown> — fixed to use generated DTOs (LogoutResponseDto, UnlinkMethodResponseDto, DeleteAccountResponseDto)

workflow: Never create git tags manually when release-please manages releases — it leaves the release PR with autorelease:pending label permanently, causing all future runs to abort.
When release-please aborts with 'untagged merged release PRs', check PR labels (autorelease:pending) not just titles — the fix is relabeling to autorelease:tagged, not renaming PR titles.
Renaming 58+ old release PR titles via GitHub API did not fix the release-please abort; the actual fix was relabeling PR #306 from autorelease:pending to autorelease:tagged.
release-please bootstrap-sha only affects commit scanning, not merged PR scanning — it does not prevent old release PRs from being matched.
fix(ci) commit type triggers a patch version bump via release-please; chore(ci) does not — choose accordingly based on whether a version bump is desired.
The Tag Staging Release workflow is manual by design — it runs E2E tests and waits for staging-approval before creating the staging-rc tag that triggers deployment.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate after inactivity; 503 errors during dashboard provisioning in the deploy workflow are transient and can be re-run without investigating further.

friction: release-please was blocked for many iterations due to the combination of: manual tag creation leaving autorelease:pending, old pre-monorepo PR titles not matching new title pattern, and bootstrap-sha not helping with PR matching — took ~10 PRs and many workflow re-runs to fully unblock

The root cause of release-please failure (autorelease:pending label on PR #306) was only discovered after exhausting title-renaming, bootstrap-sha, branch deletion, and custom title pattern approaches
release-please has no workflow_dispatch trigger, requiring a real commit push to main to re-run — needed several trivial fix PRs just to trigger new runs
axios-mock-adapter integration with vitest required multiple test rewrites before getting the interceptor tests to pass correctly
The CI verify step was comparing entire packages/api-client/ directory instead of just generated paths, causing false positives on any manual edits
open_items: React Query cache is not cleared on logout or token refresh failure (onRefreshFailure only calls clearAllUserStores, not queryClient.clear()) — noted as follow-up from CodeRabbit review on PR #309

release-please pull-request-title-pattern still needs to be set to something that doesn't rely on ${component} (e.g., 'chore: release v${version}') and PR #315 needs to be renamed to match — was in progress at transcript end
Tag Staging Release workflow for v0.25.1 was triggered but Grafana provisioning failed with 503; dashboard provisioning may need to be re-run
The IPNS SDK batch handling was mentioned as a potential performance issue separate from the DHT fire-and-forget fix — not investigated
packages/crypto has no explicit release-please entry and is not in extra-files after the fix — its version may drift from the monorepo root unless managed independently
